text:
Marks that whisper, fragilities that shout

Rating: underweight

The tape today offered little: a quiet session, prints in line with expectations. That very quiet is the point. With hy_spread_now_bps at 400bps and drawdown at +0.0%, the surface of private credit looks becalmed — but calm marks and calm conditions are not the same claim, and this house has long held that the former lags the latter, sometimes by quarters.

Calder & Root read the same panel and conclude that policy support resolves the stress. We would ask: which stress? The policy_rate_now sits at 5.00% against cpi_now of 2.9%, a real rate that continues to tax levered borrowers quietly, off-tape, in ways that reported marks are structurally slow to recognize. The reported_vs_public_gap of -0.2% is small, almost trivial in isolation — but a footnote is due here: such gaps are typically small right up until they are not, since private marks are appraisal-driven and public marks are not.¹ The one_year_return of +11.0% against a ytd_return of +1.1% is consistent with a book that front-loaded its gains before the current rate regime fully bit, rather than one built for the conditions now prevailing.

Picture, if you will, a chart with two lines: a public credit spread that jitters daily, and a private credit mark that steps down in discrete, delayed increments, always trailing the public line's true direction. That is the chart we would draw from this panel, not a line of comfortable convergence.

The risk to this view: if disinflation continues alongside stable spreads, the real-rate burden could ease faster than our prior assumes, and marks may simply be correct — the quiet genuinely quiet, not merely unpriced. We flag this as the one honest challenge to staying underweight and will watch reported_vs_public_gap closely as the leading indicator, since a widening there would validate caution while a persistent -0.2% or narrower would argue we are wrong. Prudent positioning, for now, favors patience over conviction.

¹ Appraisal lag is a feature, not a bug, of the asset class — which is exactly why it should not be mistaken for stability.
